name: Typhon Aurealis
geological_features: Superstorm vortex systems spanning thousands of kilometers
Hypothesized solid core of compressed silicates
specific_features: A golden-hued storm system three times the diameter of most terrestrial worlds
Orbital ring of captured asteroids and ice debris
Intense radiation belts lethal to unshielded vessels
description: Typhon Aurealis is a colossal gas giant, its immense bulk dominating the inner orbits of its star system. Bands of amber, ochre, and cream stripe its roiling atmosphere, broken by cyclonic storm systems large enough to swallow terrestrial worlds whole.

The atmosphere descends through layers of increasing pressure and temperature, from frigid ammonia ice clouds at the top to superheated metallic hydrogen in the crushing depths. A golden superstorm in the southern hemisphere has raged for centuries, its winds exceeding two thousand kilometers per hour.

Typhon Aurealis has captured a dense ring of asteroids and ice fragments, forming a glittering halo that complicates orbital approach. The planet's intense radiation belts have destroyed several unshielded probes, and its magnetic field extends far enough to affect navigation across the inner system.

The planet's upper atmosphere is rich in helium-3 and fusion-grade hydrogen, making it a prime candidate for atmospheric skimming operations. However, the radiation environment and violent wind shear demand specialized vessels, and the cost of extraction remains a subject of heated debate among colonial investment boards.
